blocks.text: אַם שַׁבָּת ווירד דאַז אונטענשטעהענדע הכל יודוך געבעטעט.
blocks.layout: Rashi type, one centered line; Judeo-German in Hebrew letters; only שַׁבָּת is pointed (and the patah on אַם, דאַז)

blocks.text: הַמֵּאִיר לָאָֽרֶץ וְלַדָּרִים עָלֶֽיהָ בְּרַחֲמִים. וּבְטוּבוֹ מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל־יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית: מָה רַבּוּ מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ יְיָ. כֻּלָּם בְּחָכְמָה עָשִֽׂיתָ. מָלְאָה הָאָֽרֶץ קִנְיָנֶֽךָ: הַמֶּֽלֶךְ הַמְּרוֹמָם לְבַדּוֹ מֵאָז. הַמְשֻׁבָּח וְהַמְפֹאָר וְהַמִּתְנַשֵּׂא מִימוֹת עוֹלָם: אֱלֹהֵי עוֹלָם בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ הָרַבִּים רַחֵם עָלֵֽינוּ. אֲדוֹן
blocks.layout: one indented prose paragraph, 6 lines; breaks off at אֲדוֹן (continues on the next page); a horizontal rule follows
Rashi type, centered below the rule

blocks.text: הַכֹּל יוֹדֽוּךָ וְהַכֹּל יְשַׁבְּחֽוּךָ. וְהַכֹּל יֹאמְרוּ אֵין קָדוֹשׁ כַּייָ: הַכֹּל יְרוֹמְמֽוּךָ סֶּֽלָה יוֹצֵר הַכֹּל. הָאֵל הַפּוֹתֵֽחַ בְּכָל־יוֹם דַּלְתוֹת שַׁעֲרֵי מִזְרָח: וּבוֹקֵֽעַ חַלּוֹנֵי רָקִֽיעַ. מוֹצִיא חַמָּה מִמְּקוֹמָהּ וּלְבָנָה מִמְּכוֹן שִׁבְתָּהּ: וּמֵאִיר לָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ וּלְיוֹשְׁבָיו. שֶׁבָּרָא בְּמִדַּת רַחֲמִים: הַמֵּאִיר לָאָֽרֶץ וְלַדָּרִים עָלֶֽיהָ בְּרַחֲמִים. וּבְטוּבוֹ מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל־יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית: הַמֶּֽלֶךְ הַמְּרוֹמָם לְבַדּוֹ מֵאָז. הַמְשֻׁבָּח וְהַמְפֹאָר וְהַמִּתְנַשֵּׂא מִימוֹת עוֹלָם: אֱלֹהֵי עוֹלָם בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ הָרַבִּים רַחֵם עָלֵֽינוּ. אֲדוֹן עֻזֵּֽנוּ צוּר מִשְׂגַּבֵּֽנוּ. מָגֵן יִשְׁעֵֽנוּ מִשְׂגָּב בַּעֲדֵֽנוּ: אֵין כְּעֶרְכְּךָ וְאֵין זוּלָתֶֽךָ. אֶֽפֶס בִּלְתֶּֽךָ וּמִי דּֽוֹמֶה־לָּךְ: אֵין כְּעֶרְכְּךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה. וְאֵין זוּלָתְךָ מַלְכֵּֽנוּ לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא: אֶֽפֶס בִּלְתְּךָ גּוֹאֲלֵֽנוּ לִימוֹת הַמָּשִֽׁיחַ. וְאֵין דּֽוֹמֶה־לְּךָ מוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ לִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים:

blocks.text:
אֵל אָדוֹן עַל כָּל־הַמַּעֲשִׂים. בָּרוּךְ וּמְבֹרָךְ בְּפִי כָּל־נְשָׁמָה:
גָּדְלוֹ וְטוּבוֹ מָלֵא עוֹלָם. דַּֽעַת וּתְבוּנָה סֹבְבִים אוֹתוֹ:
הַמִּתְגָּאֶה עַל־חַיּוֹת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ. וְנֶהְדָּר בְּכָבוֹד עַל־הַמֶּרְכָּבָה:

blocks.text: 37 Morning Prayer for the New Year 37
blocks.layout: centered running head, page numbers at both sides

blocks.text: On the Sabbath הכל יודוך which is printed below, is said here.
blocks.layout: italic, centered; the Hebrew is an embedded cue

blocks.text: He who lights the earth and those who dwell on it, with mercy and daily in His goodness constantly renews the work of creation. How numerous are Thy works, O Lord, all of them hast Thou made with wisdom, the earth is full of Thy possessions. O King, who alone is exalted from of old, extolled and praised and glorified since days of antiquity. O God of eternity, in Thy great mercy have mercy upon us,
blocks.layout: one paragraph, 7 lines, led by the Hebrew cue המאיר; ends with a comma (continues on the next page); a horizontal rule follows

blocks.text: All thank Thee, all praise Thee, all say: None is holy like the Lord. All exalt Thee, Selah, Creator of all, God who opens daily the portals of the Eastern gates and throws open windows of the firmament, brings forth the sun from its place and the moon from the site of its dwelling. He illuminates the whole world and its inhabitants whom He created through the attribute of mercy. He illuminates the earth and those who dwell on it with mercy, and in His goodness renews daily and constantly the work of creation. O King, who alone is exalted from of old, extolled and praised and glorified since days of antiquity. O God of eternity, in Thy great mercy have mercy upon us, Lord of our might, Rock of our fortress, shield of our salvation, a fortress around us. None can be compared with Thee, there is none except Thee, none beside Thee, and who resembles Thee? None can be compared with Thee, O Lord our God, in this world and there is none except Thee, our King, in the life of the future world. There will be nought besides Thee, our Redeemer, in the days of the anointed one and none resembles Thee, our Helper, at the revival of the dead.
blocks.layout: one paragraph, 20 lines, led by the Hebrew cue הכל יודוך; hyphenated at the line break illumi-|nates (joined here)

observations: Both pages are printed page 37. The top section is the weekday continuation of המאיר. The bottom section, set off by a rule, is the Sabbath alternative הכל יודוך followed by the start of אל אדון.
Both top paragraphs, Hebrew and English, end mid-text at אֲדוֹן / 'upon us,'. The continuation is presumably on page 38.
The Hebrew instructions are in Judeo-German written in Rashi type (Hebrew letters), not in English.
אל אדון is an alphabetical acrostic: the Hebrew lines on this page start their half-lines with א ב ג ד ה ו. No acrostic letters are marked separately in the print.
The divine Name is abbreviated as יְיָ / כַּייָ throughout, rendered 'Lord' in the English.
The English uses Hebrew cues (המאיר, הכל יודוך, אל אדון) unpointed; they link to the Hebrew paragraphs and are not part of the translation text.
The English 'Hayoth' and 'Merkabah' are capitalized as printed.
